entries.task_id: it|is|a young language
entries.description: It is a young language
entries.subject: It

spans.text: It is a young language, which only emerged in the 1970s from pervasive code-switching practices.

entries.task_id: and vp|can|be observed
entries.description: and VP can be observed
entries.subject: and VP

spans.text: A structural split between the NP and VP can be observed, with Gurindji contributing the NP structure including case-marking, and the VP structure including TAM auxiliaries coming from Kriol.

entries.task_id: including tam|auxiliaries|coming from kriol
entries.description: including TAM auxiliaries coming from Kriol
entries.subject: including TAM

spans.text: A structural split between the NP and VP can be observed, with Gurindji contributing the NP structure including case-marking, and the VP structure including TAM auxiliaries coming from Kriol.

entries.task_id: these varieties|are|similar but draw on ngarinyman and bilinarra
entries.description: These varieties are similar but draw on Ngarinyman and Bilinarra
entries.subject: These varieties
entries.object: similar but draw on Ngarinyman and Bilinarra

spans.text: These varieties are similar but draw on Ngarinyman and Bilinarra, which are closely related to Gurindji (all three belong to the Ngumpin-Yapa subgroup of Pama-Nyungan).

entries.task_id: colonists who|were|searching for good cattle pastures
entries.description: colonists who were searching for good cattle pastures
entries.subject: colonists who

spans.text: From 1855 onwards, the traditional lands of the Gurindji and neighbouring groups were seized by colonists who were searching for good cattle pastures.

entries.task_id: the gurindji|were|multilingual
entries.description: the Gurindji were multilingual
entries.subject: the Gurindji

spans.text: Before colonization, the Gurindji were multilingual, speaking the languages of neighbouring groups with whom they had familiar and ceremonial connections.

entries.task_id: and bilinarra|provided|fertile ground for the formation of the mixed language
entries.description: and Bilinarra provided fertile ground for the formation of the mixed language
entries.subject: and Bilinarra
entries.object: fertile ground for the formation of the mixed language

spans.text: It is likely that this code-switching and a certain amount of levelling between Gurindji and closely-related neighbouring languages such as Ngarinyman and Bilinarra provided fertile ground for the formation of the mixed language.

entries.task_id: movement and|can|be considered an expression of the persistence of their ancestral identity
entries.description: movement and can be considered an expression of the persistence of their ancestral identity
entries.subject: movement and
entries.object: be considered an expression of the persistence of their ancestral identity

spans.text: Meakins (2008b: 86–87) argues that maintenance of Gurindji elements in the mixed language relates closely to the land rights movement and can be considered an expression of the persistence of their ancestral identity.

entries.task_id: language situation|has|developed in a number of ways
entries.description: language situation has developed in a number of ways
entries.subject: language situation
entries.object: developed in a number of ways

spans.text: The post-contact language situation has developed in a number of ways.

entries.task_id: outsiders it|is|usually called “gurindji” by all generations
entries.description: outsiders it is usually called “Gurindji” by all generations
entries.subject: outsiders it

spans.text: To outsiders it is usually called “Gurindji” by all generations.

entries.task_id: gurindji kriol|is|required
entries.description: Gurindji Kriol is required
entries.subject: Gurindji Kriol

spans.text: If a distinction between Gurindji and Gurindji Kriol is required, Gurindji is usually referred to as “hard Gurindji”, “rough Gurindji” or “proper Gurindji”, and Gurindji Kriol as “Gurindji”.

entries.task_id: gurindji|is|usually referred to as “hard gurindji”
entries.description: Gurindji is usually referred to as “hard Gurindji”
entries.subject: Gurindji

spans.text: If a distinction between Gurindji and Gurindji Kriol is required, Gurindji is usually referred to as “hard Gurindji”, “rough Gurindji” or “proper Gurindji”, and Gurindji Kriol as “Gurindji”.

entries.task_id: gurindji kriol|continues|to be spoken alongside gurindji and kriol
entries.description: Gurindji Kriol continues to be spoken alongside Gurindji and Kriol
entries.subject: Gurindji Kriol
entries.object: to be spoken alongside Gurindji and Kriol

spans.text: In this respect, Gurindji Kriol continues to be spoken alongside Gurindji and Kriol, and is a ‘symbiotic’ mixed language.

entries.task_id: and it|is|common to find code-switching between gurindji and kriol
entries.description: and it is common to find code-switching between Gurindji and Kriol
entries.subject: and it
entries.object: common to find code-switching between Gurindji and Kriol

spans.text: In addition, code-switching continues to be an everyday practice at Kalkaringi, and it is common to find code-switching between Gurindji and Kriol, and between Gurindji Kriol and its source languages.

entries.task_id: gurindji kriol|is|stratified
entries.description: Gurindji Kriol is stratified
entries.subject: Gurindji Kriol

spans.text: The phonological system of Gurindji Kriol is stratified, i.e.

entries.task_id: it|has|maintained separate gurindji and kriol phoneme inventories
entries.description: it has maintained separate Gurindji and Kriol phoneme inventories
entries.subject: it
entries.object: maintained separate Gurindji and Kriol phoneme inventories

spans.text: it has maintained separate Gurindji and Kriol phoneme inventories, syllable structures and phonological processes.

entries.task_id: and kriol|are|quite similar
entries.description: and Kriol are quite similar
entries.subject: and Kriol

spans.text: The phonological systems of Gurindji and Kriol are quite similar, no doubt because the cattle station pidgin developed in the Victoria River District area under the influence of Gurindji.

entries.task_id: gurindji kriol|has|a 5 vowel system
entries.description: Gurindji Kriol has a 5 vowel system
entries.subject: Gurindji Kriol

spans.text: In terms of vowels, Gurindji Kriol has a 5 vowel system.

voicing
distinction|is|made
entries.description:
voicing
distinction is made
entries.subject:
voicing
distinction

spans.text: Gurindji and Kriol source words share most consonants and no voicing distinction is made.

and

entries.subject:
and
these
entries.object: used in variation with the plosive series

spans.text: Fricatives are only present in Kriol-derived words and these are used in variation with the plosive series.

entries.description: phonological systems is more obvious in syllable structure
entries.subject: phonological systems

spans.text: The maintenance of the two phonological systems is more obvious in syllable structure.
